To be more specific, in Industrial Society and Its Future, he mentions that the system is so interwoven with what we would call enlightenment or liberal-philosophy, that attempting to "reform" it is impossible.
Let me explain, in paragraphs 51 and 52 of his manifesto, he talks about how the system MUST break down familial, traditional, and social bonds.
Why is that? Well because it prides itself on an inhuman, unfeeling "efficiency", if a bureaucrat were to get his brother a cushy government job rather than selecting the best candidate we would call it "nepotism", the system couldn't function because it would be "corrupt" and place personal loyalty over loyalty to the greater system.
Similarly, if you say "well the mere existence of technology doesn't deprive us autonomy", the answer is... well it does. How many websites do you visit that track your every move? How often are you propagandized to on youtube, television, even here on /pol/? 
Technology is interwoven in the system, we expect our phone to work if we use it, but our phone can only work if we continue to try and achieve the most "efficient" (really inhuman, robotic) system possible. The system self-replicates via technology, it's an ouroboros in a sense, we need more complex systems with less autonomy over ourselves as technology improves so we can maintain an improving rate of technological progress.
